title: Proposal: working together on CFC syndrome research

sentences.text: A proposal to work together on research into BRAF-related cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome.
We are writing to CFC International because you support families and research in CFC syndrome.
We have not met yet, and we would value your guidance.
BRAF changes in CFC syndrome are reported to work by gain of function, where the protein does too much.
Families may already take part in the CITIZEN CFC Syndrome Registry, the PATRAS registry in Europe and the RASopathies Network contact registry.
Recruiting studies include a clinical and genetic study of RASopathies, a natural history study of RASopathy cardiomyopathy and a phase 2 trial of MEK inhibitors for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
A phase 3 MEK inhibitor trial, Baby MERIT, is not yet recruiting, and an earlier phase 2 MEK162 trial was withdrawn.
One limit: several of these registries and trials enrol by syndrome and their records do not name BRAF itself.
We would propose a study on [research question about CFC syndrome], shaped with your community from the start.
Its design, sites and funding are still to be settled: [study details].

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to discussing this idea with us?
If so, we would like to learn how the CITIZEN registry or your community might take part, always with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
If this is of interest, could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you?
